title: Compatibility shim for mapping OpenAI Chat Completions to Redwood streaming + tool-call model
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a resilient compatibility shim that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions style requests (chat.messages, functions, function_call hints, max_tokens, stop sequences, stream:true) and produces responses from Redwood runtime while preserving expected OpenAI semantics for both streaming and final payloads. This ticket covers mapping request fields, producing streaming deltas that match OpenAI streaming clients, handling function/tool invocation semantics (explicit function_call, auto, restricted tool availability), structured JSON output stabilization, and edge-case behaviors (early truncation, model fallback, role/name mapping).
acceptance_criteria: Shim accepts OpenAI-style request JSON and returns a non-streaming full response identical in schema to Chat Completions v1 for a subset of models

Streaming mode produces a series of delta events that follow OpenAI streaming semantics: role tokens first if present, followed by content deltas and a final done event with finish_reason matching stop/model_max_tokens/error

Function/tool invocation is surfaced as a single final message with 'function_call' object when model returns a function call; when streaming, intermediate function_call tokens are buffered and emitted correctly
Stop sequences are honored even when using batching/prefix cache; tests exist for single and multi-stop token sets
Compatibility tests (unit + integration) covering role/name mappings, unknown role names, and missing content fields, with >=95% pass in CI
Fallback logic picks an equivalent model variant and emits a scalar compatibility header and an SDK-visible flag when fallback occurs
implementation_notes: Request mapping: map 'messages' to internal prompt format and preserve message.roles and message.name where provided; translate top-level 'max_tokens' to generation length heuristics considering Redwood tokenization

Streaming implementation: use existing streaming RPC path but translate token deltas into 'delta' objects following OpenAI delta rules. For function_call streaming, buffer function_call name until name completes then emit a function_call object in final message; if model streams 'arguments' chunked, reconstruct and emit as single string value in final function_call.arguments

Structured outputs: when model returns 'structured' content, include both the plain content and a 'structured_output' metadata block in the final response to enable both OpenAI-style text and Redwood structured parsers
Error semantics: map internal errors to OpenAI error codes/messages; include request_id in metadata; ensure partial stream terminates with 'error' finish_reason and a clear audit log link
Backward compatibility: add feature-flagged header 'X-Redwood-compat: openai_chat_v1' so we can A/B rollout and quickly revert if client regressions are detected
Performance: ensure additional mapping layer adds <1ms median overhead per request under typical steady-state path; benchmark with existing runtime-1.19 perf harness
Testing: create synthetic harness with 1) simple chat, 2) streaming content, 3) function_call auto/explicit, 4) multi-tool dispatch, 5) stop-sequence edge cases, and 6) message name role edge cases
